concept: Galaga fidelity — castes, formation, dives, tractor beam, dual fighter, arcade scoring
_why: The director asked for a rebuild closer to the original (components, animation, points, gameplay). This file's predecessor exists because iteration 3 was reported as 'all acceptance gates passed' while half its brief was unbuilt: the requirements were PROSE, so nothing could fail on them. Every requirement here is DATA with a probe name, and tests/star_swarm_galaga_gate_test.php fails when one is missing or when its probe is not asserted inside an expect(...). The probes' strictness is the chair's; the gate checks that none is absent.

sources: https://tips.retrogames.com/gamepage/galaga.html — scoring table, tractor beam, extra ships
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galaga — formations, dives, bonus stages, dual fighter
https://strategywiki.org/wiki/Galaga/Gameplay — challenging-stage structure (403 on fetch 2026-09-18; scoring corroborated by the other two)
reference.discrepancy_recorded: Extra-ship thresholds are quoted as 20,000 / 70,000-then-every-70,000 by the GitHub reference and 30,000 / 80,000 by the retrogames page. The DIP default (20,000 then every 70,000) is adopted and asserted as data; the alternative is recorded rather than silently dropped.

observability._why: Behaviour cannot be probed honestly by pixel-guessing alone. The game exposes a minimal read-only surface for tests; it must not become a second code path.

requirements.statement: Three enemy castes exist and are visually distinct, matching Galaga's hierarchy: Bee (yellow/blue), Butterfly (red/white), Boss Galaga (large, four per stage).
requirements.probe: three enemy castes are distinct|bee butterfly and boss
requirements.why: Galaga's structure is the caste system: it drives formation rows, diving behaviour and scoring.

requirements.statement: The player ship and the docked dual fighter are drawn as distinct silhouettes; the dual fighter is visibly two ships.
requirements.probe: dual fighter is two docked ships|dual fighter silhouette
requirements.why: The dual fighter is Galaga's signature power-up and must be recognisable, not a bigger single ship.

requirements.statement: Raster assets stay at zero: every sprite is drawn procedurally (canvas paths), as the current game does.
requirements.why: Keeps the module dependency-free and diffable; it is also how a 1981 pixel game is honestly imitated in source.

requirements.statement: The player may have at most two shots in flight at once, as in the arcade original; the limit is observable from the state surface.
requirements.probe: at most two player shots|shot limit
requirements.why: The shot limit is a core difficulty rule, not a detail: it is why Galaga rewards timing.

requirements.statement: Each stage opens with enemies flying in along curved entry paths — from the top and the sides — spinning, then settling into the formation grid.
requirements.why: The entry swoop is the first thing a Galaga player recognises.

requirements.statement: Once assembled the formation breathes — expanding and contracting — rather than being static.
requirements.why: Galaga's formation visibly pulses; a static grid reads as unfinished.

requirements.statement: Enemies dive out of formation along curved paths, singly, in pairs and in threes, firing as they dive.
requirements.probe: dives singly in pairs and in threes|dive attack
requirements.why: The dive is the attack; formation-only enemies would not be Galaga.

requirements.statement: A destroyed enemy produces an explosion/spin animation, distinct from a plain removal.
requirements.why: Feedback on the shot is what makes the loop legible.

requirements.statement: Bee scores 50 in formation and 80 in flight (diving).
requirements.probe: bee scores 50 in formation and 80 in flight|bee scoring
requirements.why: Arcade table. In-formation and in-flight values differ for every caste.

requirements.statement: Butterfly scores 80 in formation and 160 in flight.
requirements.probe: butterfly scores 80 in formation and 160 in flight|butterfly scoring

requirements.statement: Boss Galaga scores 150 in formation, 400 diving alone, 800 with one escort and 1,600 with two escorts.
requirements.why: Arcade table, including the escort multiplier that makes bosses worth chasing.

requirements.statement: A challenging stage awards 100 per enemy destroyed and a 10,000 perfect bonus for all forty.
requirements.why: The perfect bonus is the single largest score in the original.

requirements.statement: An extra ship is awarded at 20,000 points and every 70,000 after that, and the threshold is observable in state.
requirements.why: Recorded in reference.discrepancy_recorded: the alternative 30,000/80,000 reading exists and is not silently dropped.

requirements.statement: A stage is a cycle — entry, formation, repeated dive waves, stage clear — and difficulty ramps across stages (more enemy projectiles, faster dives).
requirements.probe: difficulty ramps with stage|dive rate increases
requirements.why: Progression is the game; a single static wave is a demo.

requirements.statement: Every fourth stage is a challenging stage where forty enemies fly preset patterns and do not fire.
requirements.probe: every fourth stage is a challenging stage|challenging stage
requirements.why: Stage 3 and every fourth thereafter in the original; it punctuates the loop.

requirements.statement: A Boss Galaga may capture the player's ship with a tractor beam, costing a life; destroying the diving captor frees the ship, which docks as a dual fighter with double firepower and a larger hitbox.
requirements.probe: tractor beam captures the fighter|dual fighter doubles firepower
requirements.why: Galaga's defining mechanic, and the reason the boss exists.

requirements.statement: Destroying the captor while it holds the fighter in formation turns the captured ship into an enemy, rather than freeing it.
requirements.probe: captured fighter turns hostile|hostile captured fighter
requirements.why: The original's sharpest rule and the reason capture is a gamble, not a free upgrade.

requirements.statement: Colliding with an enemy or an enemy shot costs a life; the player respawns with the remaining lives shown in state.
requirements.probe: collision costs a life|lives decrease on hit
requirements.why: The failure condition must be real for the score to mean anything.

spec_probes._why: Each requirement's probe (or one alias separated by |) must appear inside an expect(...) statement in tests/browser/star-swarm.spec.ts. Existence is checked mechanically by tests/star_swarm_galaga_gate_test.php; the chair reviews strictness.
spec_probes.rule: existence of the probe name or alias inside expect(...) in the browser spec

invariants._why: No sprites and no new dependency keep the module diffable. A timing sleep is a race by construction (lesson L4) and is forbidden. The assertion FLOOR (60) is the completed rebuild; the BASELINE (52) is what the 52-assertion spec already had, and it is the non-shrink rule applied to a phase. Measured 2026-09-18: a single all-or-nothing gate cannot turn green until the last requirement, so the driver's progress heuristic counted three real chunks (201 lines of product change, gate 12 -> 27) as no progress and escalated. Phases exist so acceptance is satisfiable incrementally; see --phase in tools/harpp2/gates/star_swarm_galaga_gate.php.
